entities.name: Query CTP synthase
observations: 551 aa protein; estimated molecular mass 61.8 kDa and pI 7.11.
Strong homology to reviewed bacterial CTP synthases: 67.2–67.7% identity with 97.1–98.7% query coverage; best E-values 1e-267 to 7.74e-271.
Pfam architecture includes CTP_synth_N (PF06418; residues 3–265) and GATase (PF00117; residues 301–533), supporting a bifunctional CTP synthetase/glutaminase enzyme.
Likely catalyzes ATP-dependent conversion of UTP to CTP using glutamine or ammonia as nitrogen source; exact substrate usage is inferred from homologs, not directly assayed for this sequence.
Likely participates in de novo CTP biosynthesis and pyrimidine metabolism.
Homologs are annotated as homotetramers and cytosolic enzymes; these properties are inferred for the query from close bacterial homologs.

entities.name: UTP to CTP synthesis
observations: Reference CTP synthases catalyze UTP + glutamine + ATP + H2O → CTP + glutamate + ADP + phosphate, with ammonia-supported synthesis also reported.
Associated EC number is 6.3.4.2; Rhea references include RHEA:26426, RHEA:16597, and RHEA:15889.

entities.name: De novo CTP biosynthesis
observations: The enzyme is assigned to pyrimidine metabolism and the de novo CTP biosynthetic pathway, converting UTP to CTP as the second step from UDP-derived precursor flow.

entities.name: CTP synthase domain architecture
observations: N-terminal CTP_synth_N domain and C-terminal glutaminase class-I GATase domain are present in the query sequence.
A Peptidase_C26-like Pfam hit overlaps part of the C-terminal region; in this context it is likely a related catalytic-fold annotation rather than evidence of a protease function.
